title: Coefficients over a fixed service period

blocks.text: A gas utility's planners fix the end-of-horizon effect differently from lesson 7.3.4. Instead of one window from the plan's first year, they credit every start with the same **service period**: the risk removed in the `service_years` years that follow the end of its work, whenever that is. Each year's reduction is discounted at `rate` back to the plan's first year `first_year`.

`yearly_cut(main, years, start, duration, keep)` is written for you: the lesson's yearly risk reduction, for any list of calendar years that begins at `first_year`. Write `coefficients(main, starts, first_year, duration, keep, service_years, rate)` in `coefficients.py`: a dict from each start year in `starts` to its coefficient, $k.

In the lesson's notation, write $`\text{rr}_{s}`$ as a sum: over which years $`y`$, of what $`\delta_{s,y}`$, divided by what. Remember that the reduction is 0 while the work goes on, so you may include those years or not. The tests compute the yearly reductions with `scipy.stats.weibull_min.logsf`. About six lines.

"""Run executes this file. Change the calls and see what prints. Submit grades."""
import logging

# Turn the logger up, so the `log.debug` lines of your code show under the printed lines.
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")

from coefficients import Main, coefficients

main = Main(40, 3.0, 50.0, 1_000.0)
starts = [2030, 2031, 2032]

flat = coefficients(main, starts, 2030, 1, 0.0, 5, 0.0)
print("replace, 5 service years, 0%:", {s: round(v, 2) for s, v in flat.items()})
disc = coefficients(main, starts, 2030, 1, 0.0, 5, 0.05)
print("replace, 5 service years, 5%:", {s: round(v, 2) for s, v in disc.items()})
half = coefficients(main, starts, 2030, 1, 0.5, 5, 0.05)
print("keep half the age, 5 service years, 5%:", {s: round(v, 2) for s, v in half.items()})

cases.says: undiscounted, a start in the plan's first year sums the risk removed over its service years
every start counts the same number of years after its work ends
every year's reduction is discounted back to the plan's first year, whatever the start
a reduction t years after the plan's first year is divided by (1 + rate) to the power t
